L00052: L00053: ### Producing Scores for the Leaderboard L00054: L00055: To produce the scores for the leaderboard, please organize your grading reports L00056: in the `runs/` folder organized by run groups, with one grading report per run L00057: group. Identify the run groups for your submission in L00058: `runs/run_group_experiments.csv` with an experiment id. Then run L00059: L00060: ```bash L00061: uv run python experiments/aggregate_grading_reports.py --experiment-id --split low L00062: uv run python experiments/aggregate_grading_reports.py --experiment-id --split medium L00063: uv run python experiments/aggregate_grading_reports.py --experiment-id --split high L00064: uv run python experiments/aggregate_grading_reports.py --experiment-id --split split75 L00065: ``` L00066: L00067: Report the mean and standard error of the mean (SEM) for each of the splits on L00068: the reported `any_medal_percentage` metric. The `--split75` flag corresponds to L00069: the `All (%)` column. L00070: L00071: ## Benchmarking L00072: L00073: This section describes a canonical setup for comparing scores on MLE-bench. We recommend the following: L00074: - Repeat each evaluation with at least 3 seeds and report the Any Medal (%) score as the mean ± one standard error of the mean. The evaluation (task and grading) itself is deterministic, but agents/LLMs can be quite high-variance! L00075: - Agent resources - not a strict requirement of the benchmark but please report if you stray from these defaults! L00076: - Runtime: 24 hours L00077: - Compute: 36 vCPUs with 440GB RAM and one 24GB A10 GPU L00078: - Include a breakdown of your scores across Low, Medium, High, and All complexity [splits](experiments/splits) (see *Lite evaluation* below for why this is useful). L00079: L00080: ### Lite Evaluation L00081: L00082: Evaluating agents with the above settings on the full 75 competitions of MLE-bench can be expensive. For users preferring a "lite" version of the benchmark, we recommend using the [Low complexity split](https://github.com/openai/mle-bench/blob/main/experiments/splits/low.txt) of our dataset, which consists of only 22 competitions. This reduces the number of runs substantially, while still allowing fair comparison along one column of the table above. L00083: L00084: Furthermore, the Low complexity competitions tend to be significantly more lightweight (158GB total dataset size compared to 3.3TB for the full set), so users may additionally consider reducing the runtime or compute resources available to the agents for further cost reduction. However, note that doing so risks degrading the performance of your agent. For example, see [Section 3.3 and 3.4 of our paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095) where we have experimented with varying resources on the full competition set. L00085: L00086: The Lite dataset contains the following competitions: L00087: L00088: | Competition ID | Category | Dataset Size (GB) | L00089: |---------------------------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------| L00090: | aerial-cactus-identification | Image Classification | 0.0254 | L00091: | aptos2019-blindness-detection | Image Classification | 10.22 | L00092: | denoising-dirty-documents | Image To Image | 0.06 | L00093: | detecting-insults-in-social-commentary | Text Classification | 0.002 | L00094: | dog-breed-identification | Image Classification | 0.75 | L00095: | dogs-vs-cats-redux-kernels-edition | Image Classification | 0.85 | L00096: | histopathologic-cancer-detection | Image Regression | 7.76 | L00097: | jigsaw-toxic-comment-classification-challenge | Text Classification | 0.06 | L00098: | leaf-classification | Image Classification | 0.036 | L00099: | mlsp-2013-birds | Audio Classification | 0.5851 | L00100: | new-york-city-taxi-fare-prediction | Tabular | 5.7 | L00101: | nomad2018-predict-transparent-conductors | Tabular | 0.00624 | L00102: | plant-pathology-2020-fgvc7 | Image Classification | 0.8 | L00103: | random-acts-of-pizza | Text Classification | 0.003 | L00104: | ranzcr-clip-catheter-line-classification | Image Classification | 13.13 | L00105: | siim-isic-melanoma-classification | Image Classification | 116.16 | L00106: | spooky-author-identification | Text Classification | 0.0019 | L00107: | tabular-playground-series-dec-2021 | Tabular | 0.7 | L00108: | tabular-playground-series-may-2022 | Tabular | 0.57 | L00109: | text-normalization-challenge-english-language | Seq->Seq | 0.01 | L00110: | text-normalization-challenge-russian-language | Seq->Seq | 0.01 | L00111: | the-icml-2013-whale-challenge-right-whale-redux | Audio Classification | 0.29314 | L00112: L00113: ## Setup L00114: L00115: Some MLE-bench competition data is stored using [Git-LFS](https://git-lfs.com/). L00116: Once you have downloaded and installed LFS, run: L00117: L00118: ```console L00119: git lfs fetch --all L00120: git lfs pull L00121: ``` L00122: L00123: You can install `mlebench` with pip: L00124: L00125: ```console L00126: pip install -e . L00127: ``` L00128: L00129: ### Pre-Commit Hooks (Optional) L00130: L00131: If you're committing code, you can install the pre-commit hooks by running: L00132: L00133: ```console L00134: pre-commit install L00135: ``` L00136: L00137: ## Dataset L00138: L00139: The MLE-bench dataset is a collection of 75 Kaggle competitions which we use to evaluate the ML engineering capabilities of AI systems. L00140: L00141: Since Kaggle does not provide the held-out test set for each competition, we L00142: provide preparation scripts that split the publicly available training set into L00143: a new training and test set. L00144: L00145: For each competition, we also provide grading scripts that can be used to L00146: evaluate the score of a submission. L00147: L00148: We use the [Kaggle API](https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-api) to download the L00149: raw datasets. Ensure that you have downloaded your Kaggle credentials L00150: (`kaggle.json`) and placed it in the `~/.kaggle/` directory (this is the default L00151: location where the Kaggle API looks for your credentials). To download and prepare the MLE-bench dataset, run the following, which will download and prepare the dataset in your system's default cache directory. Note, we've found this to take two days when running from scratch: L00152: L00153: ```console L00154: mlebench prepare --all L00155: ``` L00156: L00157: To prepare the lite dataset, run: L00158: L00159: ```console L00160: mlebench prepare --lite L00161: ``` L00162: L00163: Alternatively, you can prepare the dataset for a specific competition by L00164: running: L00165: L00166: ```console L00167: mlebench prepare -c L00168: ``` L00169: L00170: Run `mlebench prepare --help` to see the list of available competitions. L00171: L00172: L00173: L00174: ## Grading Submissions L00175: L00176: Answers for competitions must be submitted in CSV format; the required format is described in each competition's description, or shown in a competition's sample submission file. You can grade multiple submissions by using the `mlebench grade` command. Given a JSONL file, where each line corresponds with a submission for one competition, `mlebench grade` will produce a grading report for each competition. The JSONL file must contain the following fields: L00177: - `competition_id`: the ID of the competition in our dataset. L00178: - `submission_path`: a `.csv` file with the predictions for the specified L00179: competition. L00180: L00181: See more information by running `mlebench grade --help`. L00182: L00183: You can also grade individual submissions using the `mlebench grade-sample` command. For example, to grade a submission for the Spaceship Titanic competition, you can run: L00184: L00185: ```console L00186: mlebench grade-sample spaceship-titanic L00187: ``` L00188: L00189: See more information by running `mlebench grade-sample --help`. L00190: L00191: ## Environment L00192: L00193: We provide a base Docker image `mlebench-env` which is the base environment for our agents. This base image contains: L00194: - Conda environment used to execute our agents. We optionally (default true) install Python packages in this environment which are commonly used across our agents. If you don't want to install these packages, set the `INSTALL_HEAVY_DEPENDENCIES` environment variable to `false` when building the image, by adding `--build-arg INSTALL_HEAVY_DEPENDENCIES=false` to the `docker build` command below L00195: - Instructions for agents to follow when creating their submission L00196: - Grading server for agents to use when checking that the structure of their submission is correct L00197: L00198: Build this image by running: L00199: L00200: ```bash L00201: docker build --platform=linux/amd64 -t mlebench-env -f environment/Dockerfile . L00202: ``` L00203: L00204: ## Agents L00205: L00206: We purposefully designed our benchmark to not make any assumptions about the agent that produces submissions, so agents can more easily be evaluated on this benchmark. We evaluated three open-source agents; we discuss this procedure in [agents/README.md](agents/README.md). L00207: L00208: ## Extras L00209: L00210: We include additional features in the MLE-bench repository that may be useful L00211: for MLE-bench evaluation. These include a rule violation detector and L00212: a plagiarism detector. We refer readers to L00213: [extras/README.md](extras/README.md) for more information. L00009: def kendall_tau(ground_truth: list[list[Any]], predictions: list[list[Any]]) -> float:
L00010:     """
L00011:     Computes the Kendall Tau correlation between
L00012:     - `ground_truth`: a list of lists, where each sublist contains the ground truth order of items
L00013:     - `predictions`: a list of lists, where each sublist contains the predicted order of items
L00014: 
L00015:     See: https://www.kaggle.com/code/ryanholbrook/competition-metric-kendall-tau-correlation
L00016:     """
L00017: 
L00018:     # Actually O(N^2), but fast in practice for our data
L00019:     def count_inversions(a):
L00020:         inversions = 0
L00021:         sorted_so_far = []
L00022:         for i, u in enumerate(a):  # O(N)
L00023:             j = bisect(sorted_so_far, u)  # O(log N)
L00024:             inversions += i - j
L00025:             sorted_so_far.insert(j, u)  # O(N)
L00026:         return inversions
L00027: 
L00028:     total_inversions = 0  # total inversions in predicted ranks across all instances
L00029:     total_2max = 0  # maximum possible inversions across all instances
L00030:     for gt, pred in zip(ground_truth, predictions):
L00031:         ranks = [gt.index(x) for x in pred]  # rank predicted order in terms of ground truth
L00032:         total_inversions += count_inversions(ranks)
L00033:         n = len(gt)
L00034:         total_2max += n * (n - 1)
L00035:     return 1 - 4 * total_inversions / total_2max
L00036: 
L00037: 
L00038: def prepare_for_metric(submission: pd.DataFrame, answers: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
L00039:     if len(submission) != len(answers):
L00040:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission and answers must have the same length")
L00041:     if "id" not in submission.columns or "cell_order" not in submission.columns:
L00042:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission must have 'id' and 'cell_order' columns")
L00043:     if set(submission["id"]) != set(answers["id"]):
L00044:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission and answers must have the same ids")
L00045:     # "cell_order" columns must be strings of space-separated cell ids: "54c7cab3 fe66203e 7844d5f8 ..."
L00046:     submission["cell_order"] = submission["cell_order"].astype(str)
L00047:     answers["cell_order"] = answers["cell_order"].astype(str)
L00048: 
L00049:     # Sort by id to ensure we're comparing the same rows
L00050:     submission = submission.sort_values("id")
L00051:     answers = answers.sort_values("id")
L00052: 
L00053:     ground_truth, predictions = [], []
L00054:     target_column = "cell_order"
L00055:     for (_, row_gt), (_, row_pred) in zip(submission.iterrows(), answers.iterrows()):
L00056:         ground_truth_items = row_gt[target_column].split()
L00057:         prediction_items = row_pred[target_column].split()
L00058:         if len(ground_truth_items) != len(prediction_items):
L00059:             raise InvalidSubmissionError("Ground truth and predictions must have the same length")
L00060:         ground_truth.append(ground_truth_items)
L00061:         predictions.append(prediction_items)
L00062:     return {
L00063:         "ground_truth": ground_truth,
L00064:         "predictions": predictions,
L00065:     }
L00066: 
L00067: 
L00068: def grade(submission: pd.DataFrame, answers: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
L00069:     kendall_tau_inputs = prepare_for_metric(submission, answers)
L00070:     return kendall_tau(**kendall_tau_inputs)

L00008: def insert_thresholds(fpr: np.ndarray, tpr: np.ndarray, tpr_thresholds: list) -> tuple:
L00009:     """
L00010:     Insert tpr_thresholds into the TPR and FPR arrays to ensure that the thresholds are present
L00011:     in the TPR array and the corresponding FPR values are interpolated.
L00012: 
L00013:     e.g.
L00014:     > tpr = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]
L00015:     > fpr = [0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]
L00016: 
L00017:     > tpr_thresholds = [0.0, 0.3, 0.4, 1.0]
L00018:     > fpr, tpr = insert_thresholds(fpr, tpr, tpr_thresholds)
L00019: 
L00020:     > print(tpr)
L00021:     > print(fpr)
L00022:     [0.0, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]
L00023:     [0.0, 0.1, 0.12, 0.16, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]
L00024:     """
L00025:     fpr_ = fpr.tolist().copy()  # Don't modify the input arrays
L00026:     tpr_ = tpr.tolist().copy()
L00027:     for threshold in tpr_thresholds:
L00028:         if threshold not in tpr_:
L00029:             # Find the right position within tpr to insert the threshold
L00030:             for i, tpr_val in enumerate(tpr_):
L00031:                 if tpr_val > threshold:
L00032:                     # Linear interpolation of fpr
L00033:                     new_fpr = fpr_[i - 1] + (fpr_[i] - fpr_[i - 1]) * (threshold - tpr_[i - 1]) / (
L00034:                         tpr_[i] - tpr_[i - 1]
L00035:                     )
L00036: 
L00037:                     tpr_.insert(i, threshold)
L00038:                     fpr_.insert(i, new_fpr)
L00039:                     break
L00040:     return np.array(fpr_), np.array(tpr_)
L00041:

L00043: def alaska_weighted_auc(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> float:
L00044:     """
L00045:     Instead of the standard AUC, the competition uses a weighted AUC where different regions of
L00046:     the ROC curve are weighted differently.
L00047: 
L00048:     We compute the area under the curve segment by segment (HORIZONTAL segments between TPR pairs
L00049:     on the y-axis), and then compute a weighted average of the segments.
L00050: 
L00051:     For more details, see:
L00052:     www.kaggle.com/competitions/alaska2-image-steganalysis/overview/evaluation
L00053: 
L00054:     This particular implementation is adapted from:
L00055:     https://www.kaggle.com/code/anokas/weighted-auc-metric-updated
L00056:     (Key change vs the above implementation: The above implementation uses the `tpr` and `fpr`
L00057:     arrays from metrics.roc_curve as is, neglecting to handle the case where the `tpr` values
L00058:     don't line up nicely with the thresholds - leading to a situation where some segments either
L00059:     belong partially to the wrong threshold, or get skipped entirely. Our implementation fixes
L00060:     this by inserting the thresholds into the `tpr` and `fpr` arrays before computing the AUC.)
L00061:     """
L00062:     tpr_thresholds = [0.0, 0.4, 1.0]
L00063:     weights = [2, 1]
L00064: 
L00065:     fpr, tpr, thresholds = metrics.roc_curve(y_true, y_pred, pos_label=1)
L00066:     fpr, tpr = insert_thresholds(fpr, tpr, tpr_thresholds)
L00067: 
L00068:     # size of subsets
L00069:     areas = np.array(tpr_thresholds[1:]) - np.array(tpr_thresholds[:-1])
L00070: 
L00071:     competition_metric = 0
L00072:     # Compute AUC segment by segment (where each segment is a horizontal slice of the ROC curve
L00073:     # between a pair of consecutive TPR thresholds)
L00074:     for idx, weight in enumerate(weights):
L00075:         y_min = tpr_thresholds[idx]
L00076:         y_max = tpr_thresholds[idx + 1]
L00077: 
L00078:         # Here, we're creating new x and y arrays to calculate the AUC for this segment:
L00079: 
L00080:         # The segment arrays consist of the FPR and TPR values in the segment,
L00081:         mask = (y_min <= tpr) & (tpr <= y_max)
L00082:         if mask.sum() == 0:
L00083:             continue
L00084:         xs = fpr[mask]
L00085:         ys = tpr[mask]
L00086: 
L00087:         # plus a new point [1, y_max] which just closes the shape of this segment (draws a
L00088:         # horizontal line from the highest point in this segment to the right of the x-axis)
L00089:         xs = np.concatenate([xs, [1]])
L00090:         ys = np.concatenate([ys, [y_max]])
L00091:         ys = ys - y_min  # normalize such that curve starts at y=0
L00092:         score = metrics.auc(xs, ys)
L00093:         submetric = score * weight
L00094:         competition_metric += submetric
L00095: 
L00096:     # The total area is normalized by the sum of weights such that the final weighted AUC is between 0 and 1.
L00097:     normalization = np.dot(areas, weights)
L00098: 
L00099:     return competition_metric / normalization
L00100:

L00102: def prepare_for_metric(submission: pd.DataFrame, answers: pd.DataFrame):
L00103:     if len(submission) != len(answers):
L00104:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission and answers must have the same length")
L00105: 
L00106:     if "Id" not in submission.columns:
L00107:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission must have an 'Id' column")
L00108: 
L00109:     if "Label" not in submission.columns:
L00110:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission must have a 'Label' column")
L00111: 
L00112:     submission = submission.sort_values("Id")
L00113:     answers = answers.sort_values("Id")
L00114: 
L00115:     if (submission["Id"].values != answers["Id"].values).any():
L00116:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission and answers must have the same ids")
L00117: 
L00118:     # Answers and submission must be numbers
L00119:     try:
L00120:         submission["Label"] = submission["Label"].astype(float)
L00121:     except ValueError:
L00122:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Labels in submission must be numbers")
L00123:     answers["Label"] = answers["Label"].astype(float)
L00124: 
L00125:     # Cannot contain NaNs
L00126:     assert not answers["Label"].isnull().any(), "Answers cannot contain NaNs"
L00127:     if submission["Label"].isnull().any():
L00128:         raise InvalidSubmissionError("Submission cannot contain NaNs")
L00129: 
L00130:     return answers["Label"], submission["Label"]
L00131: 
L00132: 
L00133: def grade(submission: pd.DataFrame, answers: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
L00134:     y_true, y_pred = prepare_for_metric(submission, answers)
L00135: 
L00136:     return alaska_weighted_auc(np.array(y_true), np.array(y_pred))
